name: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Pashalik of Belgrade and the districts around it, taken by the insurgents of the First Serbian Uprising

successors.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)
successors.text: Serbia in its 1913 borders with Vojvodina (24-25 November 1918) and Montenegro (absorbed on 28 November 1918); on 1 December 1918 Serbia united with the newly created State of Slovenes, Croats and…

ledger.x: 1804: the Orašac Assembly elects Karađorđe and the Serbs rise against Ottoman rule.
1805: Karađorđe proclaims Smederevo the capital in November 1805 ('proclaimed Smederevo the capital in November 1805').
1806: Belgrade falls and the insurgents control the whole Pashalik of Belgrade.

1807: Karađorđe proclaims Belgrade the capital on 8 January ('on 8 January 1807... proclaimed Belgrade the capital of Serbia'); the Porte 'first officially recognized the state as autonomous in January 1807' and the alliance with Russia followed on 10 July 1807.
1813: the Ottomans crush the uprising and retake Belgrade in October.
1815: the state is now the Principality of Serbia, recognised by the Sublime Porte; a vassal state of the Ottoman Empire until de jure independence…
1815: Miloš Obrenović raises the Second Serbian Uprising at Takovo on 23 April 1815 and wins the Pashalik of Belgrade back; the Porte's recognition is dated 1815 on the Principality page.
1833: the principality expands to the east, south and west.
1877: Serbia declares war again on 14 December and takes Niš, Pirot, Leskovac and Vranje.
1878: the Treaty of Berlin of 13 July 1878 ends the contest; Serbia's war lasted to 5 February.
1878: Serbia wins independence and the Niš lands.
1882: Serbia becomes a kingdom.
1885: Serbia attacks Bulgaria over the union of Bulgaria with Eastern Rumelia.

1886: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the Serbo-Bulgarian War with no change of frontier: 'leaving the Serbo-Bulgarian border precisely where it had been prior to the war'; 'The peace treaty was signed on February 19, 1886, in Bucharest.'
1912: the Serbian army overruns Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the Sandžak.
1912: the Serbian army takes the Albanian coast.

1913: the First Balkan War ends on 30 May 1913 (Treaty of London); Serbia keeps Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the eastern half of the Sandžak, and the occupation of these lands becomes annexation (next event).
1913: Serbia annexes Kosovo, central Vardar Macedonia and 'the eastern half of the Sanjak of Novi-Pazar'.
1913: Bulgaria attacks Serbia and Greece on 16 June 1913 and the Second Balkan War begins.
1913: the Treaty of Bucharest is concluded on 10 August 1913; the frontier follows the Vardar-Struma watershed and 'the upper valley of the Strumica remained in the possession of Bulgaria'.
1913: Serbia keeps the Vardar Macedonia lands east of its 1912 line.
1913: Serbia leaves Albania under Great Power pressure.
1914: Austria-Hungary invades Serbia.
1914: the Serbs win the campaign.
1915: the Central Powers invade and Austria-Hungary takes Belgrade.
1915: Bulgaria occupies southern and eastern Serbia and Macedonia.
1918: the Bulgarian occupation ends.
1918: the Austro-Hungarian occupation ends.
24 November 1918: Syrmia joins Serbia.
25 November 1918: Banat, Bačka and Baranja join Serbia.
1918: Serbia absorbs the Kingdom of Montenegro on 28 November ('On November 28, 1918, it absorbed the Kingdom of Montenegro').
1918: on 1 December Serbia unites with the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, the new Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.

wars.name: First Serbian Uprising
wars.outcome: The insurgents took the whole Pashalik of Belgrade by December 1806; the Porte recognised the state as autonomous in January 1807; Russia allied with Serbia on 10 July 1807; the Treaty of Bucharest of May 1812 dealt with the Serbs in Article 8; the Ottomans…

wars.name: Second Serbian Uprising
wars.outcome: Proclaimed at Takovo on 23 April 1815; in mid-1815 Miloš Obrenović negotiated with the Ottoman governor Marashli Ali Pasha; the Porte recognised the principality in 1815.

wars.name: Serbian-Ottoman War (1876-1877)
wars.outcome: Serbia declared war on 30 June 1876; 'Peace was signed on 28 February 1877 on the basis of status quo ante bellum'.

wars.name: Serbian-Ottoman War (1877-1878)
wars.outcome: Serbia took Niš, Pirot, Leskovac and Vranje (Vranje on 31 January 1878); the Treaty of Berlin of 13 July 1878 gave Serbia independence and Niš, Prokuplje, Kuršumlija, Vranje and Leskovac.

wars.name: Serbo-Bulgarian War
wars.outcome: Serbia declared war over the union of Bulgaria and Eastern Rumelia and attacked on 14 November 1885; it 'had failed to capture the Slivnitsa region which it had set out to achieve' and the fighting stopped on 28 November 1885; the Treaty of Bucharest (19…

wars.name: First Balkan War
wars.outcome: The Balkan League overran Ottoman Europe; Serbia held Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia, the Sandžak and the northern Albanian coast and withdrew from Albania under pressure from the Great Powers; the war ended 30 May 1913 (Treaty of London).

wars.name: Second Balkan War
wars.outcome: Bulgaria attacked Serbia and Greece on 16 June 1913 and lost; the Treaty of Bucharest of 10 August 1913 gave Serbia central Vardar Macedonia and Kosovo and 'the eastern half of the Sanjak of Novi-Pazar'.

wars.name: Serbian campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: 1914: Austria-Hungary invaded in August (first offensive 12 August; Cer, 'decisive defeat of Austro-Hungarian 5th Army on 20 August'), took Belgrade on 2 December and lost it on 15 December ('Serbian victory'; 28 July - 15 December 1914).

certainty.note: The frontier of the insurgent Pashalik and of the vassal principality is not given as a line by any page opened; the decrees of 1830 and 1833 enlarged it without naming districts.
Fixed by the Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878); the line itself is Cliopatria's outline, not a page.
The Albanian, Macedonian and Sandžak lands are a wartime occupation line.
Fixed by the Treaty of Bucharest of 10 August 1913 (and the Treaty of London of 30 May 1913).
Serbia is under occupation; the 1913 outline stands for its claim.
